blocks.text: So far you have spoken mainly with prepared dialogues, role-playing games and presentations. To Layer B1 you must be able to support a spontaneous conversation on family issues: answer unexpected questions, ask for clarification, express an opinion, agree or not, and especially do not block yourself when you miss a word. In this unit Luke is in Cairo, at the summer course: he speaks in Arabic standard with an Egyptian teacher and with companions from other countries, and with Laylā, arrived from Lebanon for a conference. Learn compensation strategies (description something you don't know the name of), formulas to ask, verify, take time, interrupt, agree and disagree, and natural passage between fuṣḥā and dialect. Three weeks, with many conversation sessions.

Cairo, a language institute. Time of conversation with the professor Maǧdī. With Luca there are Miguel, a Spanish student, and Yōko, a Japanese student.

rows: ⁧صَبَاحَ الخَيْرِ! اليَوْمَ سَاعَةُ المُحَادَثَةِ: لَا كُتُبَ وَلَا دَفَاتِرَ. يُوكُو،⁩ : ⁧مَجْدِي⁩ ⁧اِسْأَلِي لُوكَا عَنْ أُسْبُوعِهِ الأَوَّلِ فِي القَاهِرَةِ.⁩

I always do that too! Yesterday, I wanted to buy that sunny thing that we put on our skin...
Yōko: A cream that protects from the sun?

Maǧdī: Yes: Sunscreen is the sunscreen. Great, you help each other. Yōko- What about you? What surprised you in Cairo?
⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ تَقُولَهَا بِكَلِمَاتٍ⁩ .« ⁧فَاجَأَكِ⁩ » ⁧عُذْرًا، لَمْ أَفْهَمْ كَلِمَةَ⁩ : ⁧يُوكُو⁩ ⁧أُخْرَى؟⁩
Yōko: I'm sorry, I didn't understand the word "I"fāǧaʾaki». Can you say that in other words?
Maǧdī: Sure: what didn't you expect?
⁧وَبِكَرَمِ النَّاسِ.⁩ … ⁧آه، مَفْهُومٌ! بِصَرَاحَةٍ، فُوجِئْتُ بِالضَّجِيجِ⁩ : ⁧يُوكُو⁩ ⁧صَاحِبُ الدُّكَّانِ تَحْتَ بَيْتِي لَا يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ مِنِّي نُقُودًا عَلَى الشَّايِ!⁩
Yōko: Ah, of course! Frankly, I was surprised by the noise and generosity of people. The shop owner under the house doesn't want to get paid for tea!
⁧هٰذَا صَحِيحٌ! وَأَنَا فُوجِئْتُ بِأَنَّ النَّاسَ يَفْهَمُونَ الفُصْحَى، لٰكِنَّهُمْ⁩ : ⁧لُوكَا⁩ ⁧يُجِيبُونَ بِالعَامِّيَّةِ.⁩
It's true! And I was surprised that people understood the fuṣḥā, but answers in dialect.
⁧هٰذِهِ هِيَ القَاهِرَةُ: لُغَتَانِ فِي حِوَارٍ وَاحِدٍ! وَأَنْتُمُ الآنَ تَتَكَلَّمُونَ⁩ : ⁧مَجْدِي⁩ ⁧بِلَا خَجَلٍ، وَهٰذَا هُوَ المُهِمُّ.⁩
Maǧdī: This is Cairo: two languages in one conversation! And now you speak without shyness, and that's what matters.

blocks.text: What to notice. Strategies: Luke describes the object he cannot name ( ⁧الجِهَازُ الَّذِي يُسَخِّنُ المَاءَ⁩ ); Miguel does the same ( ⁧ذٰلِكَ الشَّيْءَ⁩ … ⁧الَّذِي نَضَعُهُ عَلَى الجِلْدِ⁩ ); Yōko calls for reformulation ( ⁧هَلْ يُمْكِنُ أَنْ تَقُولَهَا بِكَلِمَاتٍ أُخْرَى؟⁩ ) and confirms that it has understood ( ⁧مَفْهُومٌ⁩ !). ⁧كَيْفَ أَقُولُ؟⁩ It's a time-taking task. ⁧الجِلْد⁩ The skin is not exposed to the skin. ⁧الضَّجِيج⁩ The noise of the vehicle shall be: ⁧الكَرَم⁩ • generosity • ⁧الدُّكَّان⁩ The shop is in. ⁧بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا⁩ "At each other" is equal to "At each other."

In a real conversation you don't know what they're gonna ask you; You're missing a word out of ten; The other one talks faster about your book and sometimes goes to the dialect. It's not a grammar test: it's a collaboration. It matters that the message passes, that you know how to fix when something doesn't work and that the other one wants to keep talking to you. The fuṣḥā as a common language. With a teacher, with foreign students, with Arabs from different countries (a Lebanese and a Moroccan, for example), fuṣḥā is the common ground. In educated conversations one uses a fuṣḥā simplified: short sentences, few pronounced cases, many common words to dialects. This is the language of the dialogues of this unity.

blocks.text: Take time. ⁧يَعْنِي⁩ … · ⁧فِي الحَقِيقَةِ⁩ … · ⁧كَيْفَ أَقُولُ؟⁩ · ⁧سُؤَالٌ جَيِّدٌ!⁩ · ⁧دَعْنِي أُفَكِّرُ قَلِيلًا⁩ . One of these formulas gives two or three seconds to think and tells the other that you're not finished. Hold and give up the shift.

blocks.text: Mixing is not a mistake. All educated Arabs mix: a question in fuṣḥā can receive a reply in dialect, and a dialect phrase may contain a term of fuṣḥā. What matters is to remain understandable and courteous. However, avoid mixing within the same word or using the dialect in a formal writing (B1-22).
On examination B1 (part E, oral) and in real conversations the same themes always return. Prepare for each one a card with 10 keywords, 3 ready phrases and 2 questions to ask the other.

blocks.text: Luca's work. Luca just says, ⁧أَعْمَلُ فِي الشُّرْطَةِ فِي مِيلَانُو⁩ , and he gladly talks about the human side of his work (contact with people, languages, colleagues). In conversations with strangers no one is required to give details about their work: a short and friendly answer and a change of topic ( ⁧وَأَنْتَ، مَاذَا تَعْمَلُ؟⁩ ) are completely normal.

The rhythm of the conversation. In a conversation in fuṣḥā not all the endings are pronounced: we read \"in pause" the end of the groups of words. Focus on internal vowels, emphatic consonants and the intonation of questions (which rises to the end in questions yes/no: ⁧هَلْ تَتَكَلَّمُ الإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةَ؟⁩ ↗). The hesitations. ⁧يَعْنِي⁩ , ⁧فِي الحَقِيقَةِ⁩ , ⁧كَيْفَ أَقُولُ⁩ are pronounced by stretching the last vowel a bit (yaʿnīī...): it is the signal I'm thinking, I'm not finished.
